subject: Quick check: decision criteria and next steps after discovery
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Thompson <julie@habitatai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick check: decision criteria and next steps after discovery

Hi Julie,

Thanks again for taking time today — really appreciated the candid conversation about where HabitatAI is headed with model inference and the batch/real-time mix you described. A quick recap and a proposed next step so we don’t lose momentum: 

- Summary: key pain is unpredictable latency at peak (batch handling and tail latency), primary constraint is cost per 1k requests, secondary is auditability for regulated clients.
- What we showed: Redwood Dedicated options for predictable throughput, prefix caching that reduces cold-start costs, and policy-based routing to fall back to smaller variants.
- Open questions from our side: 1) target P50/P95 latency for production, 2) acceptable per-request cost envelope, 3) number of models you’d want served behind a single endpoint.

Attachments: discovery-notes-habitatai.pdf (pdf) — call notes + screenshots; pilot-outline.xlsx (xlsx) — a rough 6-week pilot we discussed.

Could you do me a favor and reply with the single most important decision criterion for your leadership team (latency / cost / compliance / other)? If you’re open, I can share a 15–30 minute pilot plan that maps to that single criterion so you can show quick ROI internally.

If now isn’t the right time, no problem — a line like “deprioritizing” is fine and I’ll close the loop.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0183

--
Redwood Inference — production-first inference for engineering teams

Date: Fri, 6 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700

Julie — following up on the note below. I know things often move slowly after an initial call, so two quick options:

1) If you have one minute: what’s the top criterion your execs will use to evaluate a vendor?
2) If you have a 15-minute window next week I’ll walk through a tailored pilot that maps to that criterion (no slides — live config + expected metrics).

If this is off the roadmap, tell me and I’ll stop nudging.

Thanks — Priyom

Hi Priyom — sorry for the delay, been buried this week. Short answer: cost is the gating factor for our CFO; latency is important but we can tolerate P95 spikes for a short pilot.

We’re pausing new vendor trials until Q4 as we focus on an internal infra refresh. Happy to revisit in October — please follow up then and send over the pilot outline so I can keep it on file.

Thanks,
